  3. Crash reports and the symbols of a build

#Crash reports and the symbols of a build

When Wren crashes, src/tools/crashtrace writes <profile>\crashes\crash <date> <time>.txt (the faulting thread's stack) and a minidump beside it (.dmp). A session that ended with no chance to write one (a fail-fast, a kill) is reported at the next start as unclean exit <date>.txt.

#What a report says

Wren 0.4.0 (g6933902 2026-10-26)

*** crash: exception (0xC000008C) at 0x7FF8A66B408A, thread 40736
  build wren.exe 6ADF67692DFE000, base 0x7FF741D90000, size 0x2DFE000
  #00 0x7FF8A66B408A RaiseException+0x8A  [KERNELBASE.dll+0xC408A]
  #01 0x7FF741D98491 ?+0x0  [wren.exe+0x8491]
  ...
  • build <exe> <fingerprint>: the build that crashed. The fingerprint is the link time stamp and the image size of the exe's PE header (%08X%X, the key a symbol server uses for an executable): every link makes a new one, and signing does not change it. base is where the exe was loaded.
  • Each frame: its address, what DbgHelp found in the process, and [module+offset]. A development, debug, check or profile build has its PDB beside it: the frames have names, files and lines. A release has no PDB (-debug would change the program: ODIN_DEBUG, the Direct3D debug layer, other code), so its own frames say ? or the nearest export, which is wrong; the offsets are what counts.

#The symbols of a build

build.bat links every variant with /MAP (it changes nothing in the exe: the sections are byte for byte the same) and tools\symbols.ps1 -Publish renames the map build\<exe>-<fingerprint>.map; a release's is also kept in build\symbols (the 20 latest). The map lists every function with its address: Odin names a procedure pkg::proc, and a private one pkg::[file.odin]::proc, so a frame gets its function and, often, its file; there are no line numbers (those need the debug information of -debug).

The map is never in what a user gets: tools\package.ps1 puts it in build\dist\symbols\<package>-<fingerprint>.map, the CI keeps it as an artifact (wren-symbols-<commit>; wren-<version>-symbols for a release, 90 days), and tools\experimental.ps1 leaves it beside the zip (and zipped in the -Vault folder).

#Naming the frames of a report

powershell -File tools\crash_symbolize.ps1 "<profile>\crashes\crash 2026-10-26 15-47-09.txt" [-Symbols <folder or .map>] [-Exe <exe with its PDB>]

It reads the build line, finds *-<fingerprint>.map (in -Symbols, the report's folder, build\, build\symbols) and rewrites each frame inside the program as function+0xoffset (file.odin) [exe+0xoffset]. A report from before the build line has only addresses: the minidump beside it gives the base and the fingerprint (its module list). Given a .dmp alone it names the exception's address. -Symbols <file.map> takes a map of another link, for instance the same commit rebuilt with the same flags: the script warns that the time stamps differ, and the Odin frames are right as long as the code is the same. -Exe uses an exe and its PDB through DbgHelp instead (files and lines; a development build).

The crash of 26/10 (an experimental build without the build line), named from its minidump and a rebuild of 6933902 with the same flags:

  #01 ... runtime.windows_trap_array_bounds+0x21  (procs_windows_amd64.odin)  [...exe+0x8491]
  #02 ... runtime.bounds_trap+0x9
  #03 ... runtime.bounds_check_error.handle_error-720+0x68
  #04 ... ui.spacer+0x316
  #05 ... browser.build_ui+0x3A8D
  #06 ... browser.frame+0x7D12
  #07 ... browser.main+0x15575

#Tests

tools\crash_e2e.ps1 (with -Ui in test_all: it needs a desktop session) builds src/tools/crashmodes as a release is built (no PDB, a map), makes it index out of range, and checks that the report has the build line and module offsets, that crash_symbolize.ps1 names crashmodes.index_out_of_range under main, and that a report without the build line is named through its minidump. src/tools/crashtrace has a unit test of the fingerprint (read in memory and from the file).
